headline: A cryptographic construction illustrates a limit of elicitation-based model capability audits
summary: The paper constructs encrypted computations that can be embedded in model weights and conditionally hidden from polynomial-time elicitation under stated cryptographic assumptions. Its PyTorch proof of concept tests a small chemistry classifier: authors report resistance to supervised fine-tuning and latent adversarial training, while 8-bit gradient-based trigger search exhaustively enumerated 256 candidates and matched random search; the evaluated 16-bit query budget remained near chance. Correct-trigger chemistry accuracy was 73.5%. The authors report individual compiled GLU units in Gemma 3 270M and a separate small experiment using Gemma 4 E4B architecture, a 64-bit trigger and 12-round Keccak-p[1600]; they do not report a full evaluation in an actual pretrained checkpoint. The v2 arXiv record states that the paper was accepted at NeurIPS 2026. They also report raw compiled weights are anomalous, while obfuscation leaves possible within-layer correlation signals. This is a conditional construction and limited experiment, not evidence of hidden capabilities in deployed frontier models.
